opinions.rationale: The interference problem is technically real, but the cloning account is imprecise. Cloning creates strategy-specific copies of each individual; it does not itself assign a realized cluster jointly. Identification fails when those individual strategies are interpreted as an infeasible or unsupported joint allocation. That is a failure of intervention definition, consistency, or structural joint positivity, not artificial censoring on an impossible world. Eligibility also need not always be cluster-dependent. The status vote concerns this technical problem and does not rely on claims about rarity or current TARGET scope.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Conventional individual-level emulations generally invoke no interference. To identify direct or spillover effects, an interference-aware emulation must specify a feasible joint or stochastic treatment policy, the potential-outcome indexing or exposure mapping, and joint support; individual clone-censor rules alone do not identify those effects.

opinions.rationale: Transporting an observational effect does require distinct treatment-exchangeability and cross-sample exchangeability conditions, together with treatment and sampling positivity. The report overstates what must be measured: identification needs a sufficient transport set, not literally every effect modifier. Effect modifiers that do not differ across samples or are irrelevant after conditioning need not all be observed. A scalar sensitivity parameter can represent an aggregate joint bias, although it cannot uniquely decompose that bias without additional restrictions. The inability to charge a discrepancy to one assumption is chiefly nonidentification, not merely absent reporting. Representation learning or site random effects do not restore identification by themselves. The empirical claim about current practice is outside this technical vote.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Transporting an observational causal contrast generally requires source treatment exchangeability and cross-sample effect exchangeability conditional on sufficient measured variables, plus treatment and sampling positivity. If either exchangeability condition fails, source outcomes and target covariates alone generally cannot identify or uniquely apportion the resulting bias without additional data or sensitivity restrictions.

opinions.rationale: The reporting concern is valid, but the stated population is wrong. Correct clone-censor weighting does not target only patients whose observed treatment remained compatible. It reweights uncensored clone-time observations to represent artificially censored observations, thereby targeting the baseline eligible population under the specified strategies, subject to exchangeability and positivity. A bare hazard ratio identifies neither an intention-to-treat nor a per-protocol strategy and may lack a causal interpretation altogether. TARGET supplies much of the reporting solution; the residual issue is adoption rather than an unresolved estimand method.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Clone-censor-weight analyses with a grace period can estimate a marginal contrast between prespecified treatment strategies in the baseline eligible population when the artificial-censoring weights and identifying assumptions are valid; when censoring enforces adherence, the contrast is per-protocol. A bare hazard ratio does not disclose the intervention, strategy, population, follow-up horizon, or intercurrent-event handling and can therefore be misread as an intention-to-treat contrast.

resolving_work.title: Transparent Reporting of Observational Studies Emulating a Target Trial: The TARGET Statement
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Provides an explicit reporting framework for the target protocol, its emulation, and effect estimates. This resolves much of the standards gap but not compliance or the incorrect subset interpretation.

counter_evidence.quote: uncensored observations are up-weighted to represent censored observations with similar characteristics and thus to allow unbiased estimation of the causal effect of interest.
the hazard ratio (HR) cannot have a causal interpretation, as it is an average of conditional time-specific effects from a cohort changing over time.
